title: Audit result
description: What the auditor returns for one artifact. Coverage is scored against the twenty-eight questions in .claude/references/filing-standard.md. The five mandatory questions each carry their own veto, so they are recorded as five independent booleans rather than folded into the coverage number.

coverage_score.description: answered / 28, as a fraction between 0 and 1. Matches the coverage field in .claude/agents/auditor.md, which writes it to two decimals.

unanswered_question_numbers.description: The filing-standard question numbers the artifact did not answer, returned to the writer. A silent rejection teaches nothing.

auditor_evidence.description: The evidence the auditor itself inspected. Same row shape as an evidence payload, so an audit is auditable on the same terms as the thing it audits.

verdict.description: REJECT releases the drum slot back to the pool. A slot spent discovering a packet was unfounded is cheaper than a packet that does not survive scrutiny.

gaps.description: Anything that could not be verified, named rather than smoothed over.

diagnostician_digest.description: The SHA-256 taken by src/integrity.js --seal after the diagnostician finished and before this audit began, copied from the .seal.json sidecar. Optional, because artifacts written before the seal existed do not carry one. When present it must equal the sidecar, and src/validateArtifact.js fails the artifact when it does not: an auditor reporting a digest other than the one taken is the case this field exists to expose.

veto_results.description: The five mandatory filing-standard questions. Each is a checkpoint with its own veto. Coverage is an aggregate, and an aggregate that can outvote a checkpoint turns the obstacle course back into an assembly line with extra steps.

q9_link_behind_claim.description: Q9. Is there a link behind the constraint claim?

q10_verify_under_60s.description: Q10. Is the verify time under sixty seconds?

q13_source_beyond_posting.description: Q13. Is the hypothesis sourced from something other than the posting alone?

q19_staged_labeled.description: Q19. Is anything staged rather than shipped labeled as staged? The Calibration Layer is the known case.

q20_agent_assisted_labeled.description: Q20. Is agent-assisted work labeled as agent-assisted?

x-rules.description: PASS requires all five vetoes true. No amount of coverage buys past a failed checkpoint.
PASS requires coverage_score at or above the current filing-standard threshold of 0.50. The threshold is a number you turn; raise it by five points every ten packets until reply rate stops improving.

coverage_score must equal (28 - unanswered_question_numbers.length) / 28, within two-decimal rounding. Coverage is countable, so a score that does not match its own unanswered list is an unscored opinion.
A PASS verdict requires at least one backstage row in auditor_evidence, or a labeled specificity leak. This is auditor.md's posting_only_rows: 0, enforced in code.

The diagnostician's half of the artifact must hash to the digest sealed before the audit ran. The auditor appends `audit` and `strikes` and changes nothing else. An artifact with no seal is reported and allowed; one whose seal does not match is refused.
